S071-01.notes: Colon plus Nobel Prize after early doubt = vindicated. Superseded/disregarded contradict the Nobel; 'work was anticipated' would mean someone foresaw her work, which is illogical here. Facts correct: maize transposition in the 1940s-50s, slow acceptance, 1983 Nobel in Physiology or Medicine.

S071-02.notes: Nesting sites tracking field drift supports magnetic-signature homing; 'may' and 'partly' are suitably hedged. A overstates (alone, ignore every other cue). B misreads: the nesting sites shifted, not the beaches. C reverses cause and effect. Brothers & Lohmann (2015, Current Biology) used 19 years of Florida nesting data; this is accurate.

S071-03.notes: Westside +100% (600->1,200), Eastside +25% (1,200->1,500). A gives the doubling (rate) and the 'still above' clause, covering both parts of the claim. B's absolute gains (600 vs 300 from a smaller base) do imply a higher rate, but only by inference, and B leaves out the 'Eastside still larger' part, so A is clearly best. C and D address only the totals. All numbers check out.

S071-04.notes: A ~14,500-year-old site contradicts 'no site much older than Clovis'. A, B and D have no support in the texts. Facts check out: Clovis ~13,000 yr; Monte Verde ~14,500 cal yr BP; the 1997 site visit by former skeptics happened.

S071-05.notes: Structure: discovery and results, then resistance, then later acceptance through germ theory. A: there are no two competing theories. C reverses the direction. D: there is no argument about training. Facts check out: 1847 Vienna General Hospital, chlorinated lime hand washing, his death in 1865, later germ theory work by Pasteur and others.

S071-06.notes: The opening modifier 'Built and expanded over many years' must attach to the nests. A attaches it to the birds, B to 'close to a ton', D to 'the weight'. Only C works. Fact is OK: communal grass nests on trees and poles, with large nests reported near a ton.

S071-07.notes: A parenthetical 'however' between subject and verb needs paired commas. B leaves the comma unclosed. C and D split subject from verb. Fact is accurate: Pteropus does not use laryngeal echolocation (unlike Rousettus) and relies on vision and smell.

S071-08.notes: The text moves from hostile water to its role as a key breeding site, so it needs a concessive transition: Even so. In other words, For example and Similarly don't fit that contrast. Facts are accurate: Lake Natron is highly alkaline and caustic, it is the main East African breeding site for lesser flamingos, and they nest on evaporite (salt) islands.

S071-09.notes: Only B gives both the conclusion and the evidence (the late eclipses at greater distance). A has evidence context but no conclusion. C has the conclusion plus a belief that came before it, but no evidence. D has neither. Facts are accurate: Rømer studied Io eclipse timings and announced the finite speed of light in 1676.

S071-10.notes: The subject is 'Each', which is singular and takes 'stands for'. The intervening 'symbols' and the 'with a single exception' phrase are distractors. 'Have stood for' is plural and the tense is wrong. Facts are accurate: Sequoyah was a silversmith, the syllabary was completed in 1821, and 's' is the only symbol that does not stand for a syllable. Literacy spread rapidly.

S071-11.notes: D is the only choice that directly contrasts the properties of gelatin and agar. A, B and C give history or current use, not why agar was better. Facts are accurate: Fanny Hesse proposed agar (from kitchen jelly-making) for Walther Hesse's lab in the early 1880s.
